basis: The Fed delivered the expected 25 bp hike to 3.75%-4.00%, but the unanimous vote and projections showing 16 of 18 policymakers expecting at least one more 2026 hike were incrementally hawkish.

The first post-decision relief move reversed during Chair Warsh's press conference: by the close the S&P 500 was down about 0.8%, Nasdaq down about 0.5%, the 2-year yield near 4.73%, the 10-year near 5.01%, and the dollar index roughly 0.6% higher.

Do not automatically extrapolate the announcement move. Penalize entries already extended multiple ATRs; require completed 5m/15m acceptance, failed-retest evidence, and distinguish continuation from reclaim/mean-reversion.

Gold and silver remain pressured by the stronger dollar and higher front-end yields, but deeply oversold RSI or bullish divergence raises snapback risk. Crude remains driven more by supply/inventory dynamics than the Fed.
After the 4:00 PM equity close, thinner liquidity and position unwinds can produce false breaks. Use structural stops and no-chase boundaries.
